A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial additions and reformatting in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ensemble-attack experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10, including attack success, loss and prediction-variance curves in Figures 2–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds CIFAR-100 results in Appendix E and Figure 6.

M1.justification: The ensemble attack objective and MLP/CNN architectures are retained. v2 identifies MI-FGSM and the losses used in existing experiments, but does not establish a changed attack procedure. Its KL-divergence and defense discussions are theoretical extensions.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds evaluated CIFAR-100 classification coverage alongside the retained MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments. This is a limited expansion to images with 100 classes. Neither version supplies reported ImageNet results despite mentioning that dataset.

E2.justification: The experimental comparisons retain the MLP/CNN ensemble configurations and ResNet-18 target. Newly cited attack and defense methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve ensemble sizes, weight-decay values and plotted attack-step ranges. v2 newly documents previously unspecified settings rather than reporting revisions to them. Appendix E explicitly follows the existing experimental setting.

E4.justification: Figure 6 extends attack-step and weight-decay sensitivity analysis to CIFAR-100, examining how attack success, loss and prediction variance respond. The existing attack-dynamics and ensemble-size analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Prediction variance measures ensemble diversity in both versions; it is not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 retain identical plotted results. v2 adds CIFAR-100 attack-success, loss and variance trajectories in Figure 6, including their dependence on weight decay. These are additional dataset results, not improvements under the original settings.

T1.justification: The main bound changes from v1 Theorem 2 to v2 Theorem 4.3: the radicand coefficient increases from 2 to 18, with an additional factor of four inside the logarithm, following added concentration and union-bound steps. v2 also adds a multiclass KL/Bregman decomposition, an information-theoretic bound, and model-distribution/domain extensions in Appendices B.3, B.5 and D.4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: transferability-error, diversity and complexity definitions; vulnerability-diversity decomposition; an error bound; and guidelines concerning ensemble size, diversity and complexity. The additional material does not replace these main scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations concerning model-specific information and overfitting, differing surrogate/target distributions, relationships between theoretical bounds, and possible ensemble-defense applications. Section 5.1 also adds an initial-phase versus potential-overfitting interpretation of the retained curves.

D1.justification: Section 5 substantially fills gaps in experimental documentation: 10/30 training epochs, Adam, learning rate 0.001, batch size 64, MI-FGSM, 20 attack steps, cross-entropy optimization and mean-squared-error measurement. v1 provided architectures and regularization values but omitted these operational details.

R1.justification: Appendices D.2–D.4 and D.8 substantially expand positioning against gradient-diversity definitions, Yang et al. (2021)'s bound, domain-adaptation theory and ensemble-defense research. New references include Kariyappa and Qureshi (2019), Blitzer et al. (2007), and Deng and Mu (2023); the Wood reference's year change concerns the same work.

P1.justification: The six main sections and much existing prose remain intact. v2 makes localized explanatory rewrites, condenses the conclusion and ethics statement, updates an affiliation, and reorganizes Appendix D while adding new appendix subsections.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column presentation, substantially altering figure placement, sizing and equation layout. Figure 5's dataset panels are restacked vertically, and Figure 6 is added. The retained plots preserve their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves experimental documentation, adds CIFAR-100 evidence, and supplies previously missing concentration and union-bound steps. However, its important theoretical additions contain unresolved inconsistencies: Proposition B.3 defines KL(f||y), while its proof uses KL(y||f), and Appendix D.4 retains v1's smaller bound constants despite citing the revised Theorem 4.3. These problems affect the claimed theoretical expansion, making the net quality change uncertain.
